steps.title: Obtain samples and initial handling
steps.instruction: Obtain IRB approval, recruit healthy male donors (>21 y) who abstain 3 days, collect fresh ejaculate by masturbation into sterile polypropylene containers (catalog 75.9922.745) free of plasticizers, record collection time, deliver to lab within 30 min, let sit at room temperature (≈24 °C) for 30–60 min, and begin swim‑up within 1 h of collection.

steps.title: Prepare HTF solution
steps.instruction: Make Human Tubal Fluid (HTF) by dissolving for 500 ml: NaCl 2.86 g, KCl 0.186 g, MgSO₄·7H₂O 24.6 mg, KH₂PO₄ 25.2 mg, CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.147 g, HEPES 3.336 g, Sodium Lactate (60 % w/w) 1.5 ml, Sodium Pyruvate 22 mg, Glucose 0.270 g; adjust pH to 7.3–7.4 with NaOH, verify osmolarity 280 ± 5 mOsm with a vapor‑pressure osmometer, filter through a sterile 0.2 µm PES filter, and store at 4 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare HS solution
steps.instruction: Make High‑Saline (HS) solution for 500 ml by adding: NaCl 3.945 g, KCl 0.186 g, CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.147 g, MgSO₄·7H₂O 0.123 g, HEPES 2.383 g, Glucose 0.451 g, Sodium Lactate (60 % w/w) 0.75 ml, Sodium Pyruvate 0.055 g; adjust pH to 7.3–7.4 with NaOH, verify osmolarity 320 ± 5 mOsm, filter through a sterile 0.2 µm PES filter, and store at 4 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare capacitation media
steps.instruction: To freshly prepared HS solution add 20 % (v/v) Fetal Bovine Serum and 25 mM NaHCO₃; use the media the same day.

steps.title: Prepare peptide stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve human fibrillogenic peptide SEM1(86‑107) to 2.5 mg ml⁻¹ in PBS (pH 7.0); peptide purity must be > 95 %.

steps.title: Generate SEM1 fibrils
steps.instruction: Aliquot 100 µl of the 2.5 mg ml⁻¹ peptide into tubes, agitate for 12 h at 37 °C, 1 400 rpm in an Eppendorf Thermomixer; solution should become turbid, confirming fibril formation (verify by thioflavin T binding or EM).

steps.title: Set up swim‑up tubes
steps.instruction: Add 7 ml warm HTF (≈37 °C) to each 50 ml centrifuge tube, then underlay 1 ml liquefied ejaculate at the tube bottom using a positive‑displacement pipette, avoiding bubbles or agitation.

steps.title: Incubate for swim‑up
steps.instruction: Place tubes in a 37 °C incubator on a stand tilted 45°, incubate 1 h; if using a CO₂ incubator, close caps tightly (CO₂ not required).

steps.title: Collect motile sperm supernatant
steps.instruction: After 1 h, carefully pipette 2–3 ml supernatant from each tube (near the surface) and pool into a single 15 ml conical tube; leave several milliliters of HTF above the seminal plasma, discard the original tubes.

steps.title: Settle and concentrate sperm
steps.instruction: Let the pooled 15 ml tube stand vertically at room temperature for 30–60 min so sperm settle as a white cloud; then remove most of the supernatant, gently resuspend the cloud in the remaining HTF to obtain a concentrated suspension.

steps.title: Determine cell concentration
steps.instruction: Take an aliquot of the sperm suspension and count cells with a hemacytometer (WHO normal ≥ 15 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹).

steps.title: Prepare recording chamber
steps.instruction: Place a 5 mm diameter coverslip in the main well of the diamond‑shaped recording chamber, fill the chamber with ~300 µl room‑temperature HS solution, ensure all wells (main and suction) are filled, and eliminate any air bubbles under the coverslip by tapping with a pipette tip or forceps.

steps.title: Add sperm to chamber
steps.instruction: Add 20–50 µl of the concentrated sperm suspension to the HS solution above the coverslip, then let sperm sediment onto the coverslip for 10–30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Optional capacitation step
steps.instruction: If capacitated cells are required, after adhesion perfuse the chamber with capacitation media and incubate 4 h at 37 °C in a 5 % CO₂ incubator; do not turn on perfusion immediately after placing a fresh coverslip to maximize cell attachment.

steps.title: Mount chamber on microscope
steps.instruction: Place ~50 µl water droplet on the 60× objective, insert the recording chamber into the stage adapter, connect perfusion and suction lines, turn on the light source, and locate the focal plane of the coverslip surface (first find an edge, then focus upward through glass, coverslip bottom, then upper surface).

steps.title: Prepare HS perfusion
steps.instruction: Ensure HS solution in the perfusion syringe is at room temperature (~24 °C); if a warmer temperature is needed, place the chamber and adapter in an incubator or use a built‑in heater.

steps.title: Assess sperm morphology and motility
steps.instruction: Using WHO guidelines, evaluate strict morphology, overall motility, and concentration; select morphologically normal sperm for video recording.

steps.title: Record control videos
steps.instruction: Switch the microscope to camera mode, activate the camera, and record videos at 1 000 frames s⁻¹ (≈1 ms per frame), selecting fields where flagella do not overlap.

steps.title: Apply treatment compounds
steps.instruction: Perfuse or pipette treatment (e.g., 50 µg ml⁻¹ SEM1 fibrils or monomeric peptide control) into the chamber, wait 10 min, then record additional videos under the same settings.

steps.title: Remove and clean coverslip
steps.instruction: After all recordings, carefully remove the coverslip with forceps and discard it; aspirate remaining solution from the chamber, rinse with water, then with 70 % ethanol, and finally perform three rinses with deionized water (18 MΩ), avoiding prolonged alcohol exposure. The chamber can be reused indefinitely.
